sections.body_md:
Going from a transfer function back to state space is the opposite of the resolvent formula, and it does not have one answer. Any matrices whose input-output map equals \(G(s)\) are a realization. A change of coordinates produces another one, with a similar \(A\) and the same poles.

The useful normal forms put the denominator coefficients in a fixed place. Controllable canonical form writes them along the last row. Observable canonical form writes them down a column. Both are valid. A realization is minimal when nothing cancels, so the number of states equals the degree of \(G\) after common factors are removed.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
For \(G(s) = (b_1 s + b_0)/(s^2 + a_1 s + a_0)\), one controllable form is
\[
A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -a_0 & -a_1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad
C = \begin{bmatrix} b_0 & b_1 \end{bmatrix}.
\]
The characteristic polynomial is \(\det(sI - A) = s^2 + a_1 s + a_0\). The DC gain of a strictly proper \(G\) is \(b_0/a_0\).

If a factor \((s-z)\) sits in both the numerator and the denominator, a minimal realization deletes it. The cancelled eigenvalue can still be placed in a larger non-minimal model, where it is unreachable or unobservable.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Take \(G(s) = (6s + 24)/(s^2 + 13s + 16)\). Then \(a_0 = 16\), \(a_1 = 13\), \(b_0 = 24\), and \(b_1 = 6\). The companion matrix has last row \((-16,\; -13)\), and \(C = (24,\; 6)\). The DC gain is \(24/16 = 1.5\). Nothing cancels, so two states are necessary and sufficient. A different basis would scramble the entries and leave \(G(0) = 1.5\) and the poles alone.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: The bottom-left entry is \(-a_0\), not \(a_0\), and not \(-a_1\). Counting states from the written denominator, before cancellation, inflates a non-minimal model. DC gain is \(b_0/a_0\) for the form above, not the ratio of the highest coefficients. And similar matrices share eigenvalues, so a change of basis cannot move a pole, even though every entry of \(A\) may change.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Reachability asks whether the input can excite every state of this realization, and observability asks whether every state appears at the output. State feedback then places the eigenvalues of \(A - BK\), which is legal in the controllable form precisely because that form was built to be controllable when nothing has cancelled.
